commands.label: Compile Java caller once against official provider

cases.evidence: Official javap records marks.JvmName on each renamed class, including import aliases and wildcard imports.
cases.resolution: Preserve canonical identity and ordinary annotation retention; exclude this case from differential pass counts. Pinned IR FileClassLowering.kt:194-197 compares the annotation constructor parent class name only; the emitted annotation descriptor proves marks.JvmName identity. This is recorded as a suspected oracle bug, not adopted as language behavior.

cases.verification: Independent canonical annotation identity and facade-name assertions

limitations: File JvmName consumes canonical annotation identity and folded String arguments; bounded ASCII identifier JVM facade names. Existing non-ASCII source filename boundary remains even with an explicit facade name. Multifile facades, source annotation type aliases and member JvmName remain unsupported.

Private/internal primary constructors of ordinary final nongeneric classes, without defaults, constructor annotations or secondary constructors. Protected, inner, value, sealed, data and open combinations retain explicit boundaries. Ordinary constructor callable references retain their existing explicit unsupported boundary.

Java callers compile once against official output and run unchanged against both providers with -Xverify:all. Kotlin consumers are compiled against each provider separately; candidate consumers are also compiled against both providers.

Custom marks.JvmName source probes expose a documented official short-name lowering discrepancy; those results are excluded from differential passes. No full Android application or performance claim. DownloadMapper and SongFilter motivate visibility but contain broader unsupported semantics.
